q1.prompt: You need ordered keys with average log n search and inorder walk. Which structure?

wrong_hash.prompt: Hash maps do not give sorted order.
wrong_hash.explanation: A BST keeps ordering so inorder is sorted and range queries work. A hash map averages O(1) but has no key order.

q2.prompt: Sorted inserts make the raw tree a chain. What should you reconsider?

choices.label: When inputs can be sorted and you promise log n with no balance story, or a hash map suffices and order is unused
Raw BSTs always guarantee log n

wrong_refuse.explanation: Avoid promising O(log n) without a balance story when inputs can be sorted. Avoid a raw BST when a hash map suffices and order is never used. Avoid deleting a two-child node by only nulling it out.

success.prompt: You matched BSTs to ordered keys and avoided unbalanced or unnecessary ones.
